emailEntry.description: One email address entry, carrying card-scoped contexts and preference alongside the email value.

contexts.description: Free-text roles this email serves, e.g. ["work"], ["home"], ["billing"] (JSContact-style) -- WHERE this email is used. Emails have no separate kind field: there is no mobile/fax-style distinction for email addresses.

preference.description: Rank among this contact's emails; 1 = most preferred (vCard PREF) -- the primary email is the entry with preference 1. Absent means unspecified -- do NOT treat missing as 100 (lowest). Consumers comparing preferences should ignore entries without a value.

linkEntry.description: One web link entry, carrying card-scoped kind, contexts, and preference alongside the URL.

contexts.description: Free-text roles this link serves, e.g. ["work"], ["personal"] (JSContact-style) -- WHERE this link is used. Kept separate from kind (WHAT the link is, e.g. "avatar"/"calendar") per this suite's contexts/kind split: contexts never carries a kind-style value.

kind.description: Open-vocabulary link kind -- WHAT this link is (a website, an avatar image, a calendar, a portfolio, a social profile), as distinct from contexts (WHERE it's used, e.g. home/work). Not a closed enum, same open-vocab pattern as platform (JSContact Link.kind precedent) -- new link kinds shouldn't require a schema change.

preference.description: Rank among this contact's links; 1 = most preferred (vCard PREF). Absent means unspecified -- do NOT treat missing as 100 (lowest). Consumers comparing preferences should ignore entries without a value.

value.description: The link URL, e.g. a website, portfolio, calendar, or avatar image.

phoneEntry.description: One phone number entry, carrying card-scoped kind, contexts, and preference alongside the phone value, plus an optional extension.

contexts.description: Free-text roles this phone serves, e.g. ["work"], ["home"], ["billing"] (JSContact-style) -- WHERE this phone is used. Kept separate from kind (WHAT the number is, e.g. "mobile"/"fax") per this suite's contexts/kind split: contexts never carries a kind-style value.

extension.description: Extension digits, e.g. "4321". The phone scalar (E.164, see contact.scalars) deliberately excludes extensions -- this is where they live, kept separate from the dialable number.

kind.description: Open-vocabulary phone kind -- WHAT this number is (a mobile line, a landline/voice line, a fax, a pager), as distinct from contexts (WHERE it's used, e.g. home/work). Not a closed enum, same open-vocab pattern as links.kind (JSContact Phone.features precedent, collapsed to a single primary kind for the 80% case) -- new kinds shouldn't require a schema change.

preference.description: Rank among this contact's phones; 1 = most preferred (vCard PREF) -- the primary phone is the entry with preference 1. Absent means unspecified -- do NOT treat missing as 100 (lowest). Consumers comparing preferences should ignore entries without a value.

description: A person or organization contact card, JSContact (RFC 9553)-shaped but trimmed to the 80% common case. emails, phones, and links each use a uniform {value, contexts, preference} entry shape; phones and links also carry an optional open-vocab kind (WHAT the entry is: mobile/fax, website/avatar) kept separate from contexts (WHERE it is used: home/work). addresses and socialHandles skip this wrapper entirely -- their items (the postal.address union, contact.social-handle) already carry contexts and preference natively, so re-wrapping them would be redundant. organization and title are flat display strings rather than references to separate entities -- the CRM 80% case doesn't need normalized org/role records. name is the only required field: names do not split universally into given/family parts across cultures, so nameComponents is optional structure layered on top of the required display name, never a substitute for it.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- a contact.card returned as a typed response body, or embedded in a card-specific field, doesn't need one. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

addresses.description: Postal addresses for this contact. References the postal.address union, never a concrete variant like us-address directly, so this schema does not need to change when new address kinds are added. No wrapper entry here (unlike emails/phones/links) -- contexts and preference live on each address variant itself (us-address, postal.au-address, and future variants all carry them), since an address's role and rank are properties of the address, not of its membership in this array.

emails.description: Email addresses for this contact. contexts says WHERE each address is used (e.g. work/home/billing); emails have no kind field. "Primary email" is the entry with preference 1 (see emailEntry).

externalReferences.description: Links to corresponding records in foreign systems, e.g. CRM contact or lead ids -- see external-reference for shape and validation. Replaces ad-hoc *Id fields scattered across schemas with one uniform array.

kind.description: Open-vocabulary JSContact-style entity kind -- what this contact IS, e.g. a person vs. an organization vs. a group vs. a bot. Not a closed enum: descriptive metadata, not a discriminator this schema branches on, so new kinds don't require a schema change.

links.description: Web links for this contact -- websites, portfolios, calendars, avatars, and similar. kind (open-vocab, e.g. "website", "avatar", "calendar") says WHAT the link is; contexts (free text, e.g. ["work"], ["personal"]) says WHERE it's used -- kept separate per this suite's contexts/kind split rather than folding both into one field.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

name.description: Display name for this contact -- the only required name field. Never require given/family name parts separately: names do not split universally into given/family components across cultures, so a single freeform display string is the reliable minimum every contact has.

nameComponents.description: Optional structured name parts, layered on top of the required name display string -- never a substitute for it. All parts are optional since not every name decomposes into given/family/middle/prefix/suffix.

organization.description: Company or organization display name, e.g. "Acme Corp". A flat string, not a reference to a separate organization entity -- CRM-style contact cards typically need only a label here, not a normalized org record.

phones.description: Phone numbers for this contact. kind (open-vocab, e.g. "mobile", "fax") says WHAT the number is; contexts (free text, e.g. ["work"], ["home"]) says WHERE it's used -- kept separate per this suite's contexts/kind split. "Primary phone" is the entry with preference 1 (see phoneEntry).

socialHandles.description: Social/messaging identities for this contact -- see contact.social-handle. No wrapper entry here (unlike emails/phones/links) -- contexts and preference live on contact.social-handle itself, for the same reason as addresses.

title.description: Job title or role, e.g. "VP of Sales". A flat string for the same reason as organization -- the CRM 80% case, not a normalized role/position entity.

title: Contact card
